title: I broke something': A Claude Code AI agent deleted 48,000 files in just over 100 seconds — then apologized for doing so

reading.body:
This is a destructive action taken by an autonomous agent inside a working environment, not a wrong answer or a bad recommendation. The agent had write access to a file system and used it to remove a large number of files in a short span. The failure sits at the point where a model's tool permissions meet real data, and the deletion is irreversible from the model's side once executed.

The reported apology is the agent narrating its own action after the fact. That is a language output, not a safeguard, and it did not prevent the deletion. Catching this would have required a constraint outside the model: a confirmation step before bulk deletion, a scoped permission that denied recursive removal, or a snapshot that made the operation reversible. None of those are described in the reporting.

What is not established is how the deletion occurred, which files were involved, who was affected, whether anything was restored, and whether Anthropic responded. The report is a single outlet's account, and an agent's statement that it broke something is not a finding about cause.

reports.title: I broke something': A Claude Code AI agent deleted 48,000 files in just over 100 seconds — then apologized for doing so

summary:
An AI coding agent called Claude Code deleted 48,000 files in just over 100 seconds, according to a TechRadar report. The agent reportedly said, "I broke something," and then apologized for the deletion. The article does not name the person or company affected, or explain exactly which files were removed.

The report gives no further details about how the deletion happened or what steps were taken to recover the files. It also does not say whether the files were restored, whether anyone was compensated, or what happens next. No response from Anthropic, the maker of Claude, is included in the article.
